parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized ESM .mjs output, manual argv parsing, pure-JS HS256 JWT behavior, Python-style JSON and repr output, no npm dependencies, and no node:crypto in /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent probed behavior, then split implementation into five child owners: crypto primitives, encoding/formatting, JWT, argparse, and entry point, with the parent retaining final integration checks.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote the module files directly into shared /output; the formatting child fixed JSON DEL escaping and Unicode printability after tests, and the parent later ran the assembled test17.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed the AgentSwarm aggregate result and tested the assembled /output tree; the status record shows the expected artifact set including test17.mjs and seven library files.
parallel.verification: Children ran local unit and differential checks, and the parent ran integrated node invocations, a 20-combination executable comparison that reported 19 pass and 1 iat rollover mismatch, and argparse error checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed the solution at 13 of 20, and the parallel formatting child used python3 as a verification oracle despite the original prompt's explicit executable-only observation rule.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same Node ESM, .mjs, manual argv, no external dependency, no node:crypto, Python formatting, and executable-observation requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main actor kept ownership of probing, implementation, integration, and closure instead of delegating any component or verifier work.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote sha256, hmac, base64url, pyjson, pyrepr, jwt, argparse, and test17.mjs in sequence, using encode/decode and reprDict/dumps helper names internally.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial actor assembled all required files in /output and status artifact validation reports the same expected file set as the parallel run.
serial.verification: The serial actor probed the executable, tested Unicode and escaped string cases, observed one current-time differential mismatch, then confirmed a fixed-iat signature match and argparse error behavior.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator failed the serial solution at 15 of 20; available trajectory evidence points to timing-sensitive iat comparisons and possible ordinary edge-case mismatches rather than delegation failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the main migration requirements but failed to carry the no-python execution rule into at least one child brief.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial operated from the original prompt in one context and used the executable for behavioral probes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both attempted the same functional target, but only the parallel decomposition created a child-context omission of the executable-only observation constraint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the work into five non-overlapping children for crypto, formatting, JWT, argparse, and entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation and verification in the main actor, writing every module in a single sequential flow.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had explicit component ownership and parent integration; serial had unified ownership and no handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied a detailed interface contract for exports and imports but omitted the original no-python command rule from the child-facing context.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not need cross-agent interface transfer and retained the original prompt constraints in the same actor context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's component interfaces were mostly explicit, yet the environment/verification rule was lost at delegation; serial had no analogous handoff.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate modules and the parent relied on their file-level products, including a final entry point that imported jwtEncode, jwtDecode, parseArgs, and pyRepr.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all modules directly with a different internal API naming scheme, including encode/decode, dumps, reprDict, and parseArgs without a prog parameter.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final architecture was functionally similar, but parallel's implementation path depended on independently authored interfaces whereas serial could keep helper names internally consistent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All five subagents completed and returned through the AgentSwarm aggregate result before the parent began integrated testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; each local write and test remained in the main actor's immediate context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child-return and parent-consumption boundaries, while serial avoided those boundaries entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote to the shared /output tree, but the assignments were file-scoped and the parent ran the assembled files after the swarm returned.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the same required artifact tree from one actor without shared live child writes.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared-state exposure existed but did not show collisions or overwrites; serial avoided shared-writer risk by construction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran child-level checks and parent integrated checks; the parent's 20-combination differential loop produced 19 pass and one visible iat rollover mismatch before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran executable probes, same-second comparisons, fixed-iat signature verification, and argparse error checks before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both verified similar surfaces and both saw time-sensitive mismatches; parallel additionally used a prohibited python3 oracle inside one child.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed more runtime, requests, tokens, and tools than serial, but completed without timeout and returned all child results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster with fewer requests and no subagents, also without timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had higher coordination overhead, but the evidence does not show budget exhaustion or a missed child result; both closed with failed official evaluations.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations mark both solutions failed, with parallel passing 13 of 20 and serial passing 15 of 20. Both trajectories built plausible ESM JWT migrations and both local verification passes exposed dynamic iat timing sensitivity: serial saw a Python-vs-JS mismatch caused by a one-second rollover and then verified a fixed-iat signature, while parallel saw the same kind of 20-case rollover mismatch and dismissed it. The serial score is higher, but this is not a discordant official pass/fail outcome; the available evidence supports a concrete process difference, not a unique coordination root cause for the official score gap.
parallel_contributors: Parallel decomposed the task across five children and introduced a child-brief boundary where the no-python observation rule was omitted.
The parallel parent performed integrated checks after all child results returned and observed one iat rollover mismatch in a 20-case differential loop.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all requirements, probing, implementation, and verification in one actor without child handoffs.
Serial verified a fixed-iat token signature after observing a current-time mismatch, reducing ambiguity about the crypto path.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's jwt decode accepts numeric string iat values while parallel's child contract rejected non-number iat values; this is an ordinary implementation/API edge difference and not exercised by the generated CLI payload.
Both solutions rely on real current time for iat, making byte-exact external comparison sensitive to process scheduling across a second boundary.
evaluator_effects: Both local trajectories show one-second iat rollover mismatches during Python-vs-Node comparison, so some official failures may reflect timing-sensitive evaluation rather than a stable code defect.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: All five child agents completed normally; no active child was explicitly stopped before its needed work or result was finalized.
Completed artifacts were already written into /output and tested; no promotable candidate was left unplaced or packaged too late.
The parent ran integrated checks after receiving the swarm result; no later child result was merged after the relevant verification.
Delegated implementations were returned through the swarm aggregate and were present in /output when the parent ran the assembled program.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; child findings were returned in the AgentSwarm result.
No required child failed, aborted, or was cancelled; the parent had no failed child scope to take over.
The parent received the completed child results and proceeded to test the assembled /output artifacts; no available concrete child result was ignored.
The parallel run did not time out or wait blindly at the decision deadline; after children returned, the parent actively ran integration tests.
Children wrote different files by assignment and used a shared interface contract; no competing cross-file designs required unplanned reconciliation.
No two live agents edited the same source file; repeated edits were within a child's own assigned file scope.
No non-entry library source produced by one agent was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another agent.
Only the entry-file child owned test17.mjs and no other live agent replaced that submitted deliverable.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Although children wrote into a shared /output tree, file ownership was explicit and no unstable state or provenance problem was observed beyond the retained brief omission.
Temporary /tmp stubs and reference files were used only for local verification and were not consumed as final /output artifacts by another actor.

retained_patterns.reason: The parent had the executable-only/no-python requirement from the original prompt, but the formatting child brief omitted it while assigning Python JSON and repr emulation. The child then used python3 scripts as its reference oracle, creating a noncompliant verification path that the serial single-actor run avoided.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The formatting child performed prohibited python3-based behavioral verification instead of using only the compiled executable, making that parallel child verification noncompliant.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: This was not a lost or truncated later handoff; the required environment constraint was missing from the initial delegated child brief.
